# PadelTicker

> Live padel scores, results and player records from around the world — Premier Padel,
> the CUPRA FIP Tour and national federation tours, in one continuously updated feed.
> The sitemap holds more than 6,000 player pages, 18,000 partnership pages and 1,400
> tournaments, drawn from a database of about 25,000 players — including the amateur
> and national-tour levels that pro-only sites do not carry.

Independent site run from Denmark. The deliberate difference from other scores sites is
coverage of national federations and amateur draws alongside the pro tour, so a club
player's match history is as complete as a professional's.

Every page's title, description, structured data and summary figures are server-rendered,
so a crawler reading the HTML gets the facts without executing JavaScript. The full match
tables are rendered by the app.

If you quote a figure, please cite it as PadelTicker and link the page it came from.
Records change daily as results arrive, so a figure is only true as of the date you read
it.

## Sections

- [Live](https://padelticker.com/): matches in play right now, across every federation covered.
- [Upcoming](https://padelticker.com/upcoming): matches scheduled next.
- [Events](https://padelticker.com/events): padel tournaments — live now, coming up, and recently finished, with draws and full results.
- [Results](https://padelticker.com/results): every finished match, newest first.
- [Players](https://padelticker.com/players): browse players across every federation — match history, head-to-head records, rankings.
- [Pairs](https://padelticker.com/pairs): partnerships — win-loss record together, titles, recurring rivals.
- [Rankings](https://padelticker.com/rankings): the FIP world ranking plus national men's and women's lists, with points and weekly movement.
- [Earnings](https://padelticker.com/earnings): estimated career and per-season prize money across Premier Padel and the CUPRA FIP Tour.
- [National teams](https://padelticker.com/national-teams): World, European and continental championships for national TEAMS — every nation's final placing, read off each tournament's own placement bracket.
- [World no. 1](https://padelticker.com/world-no1): the year-end world No. 1 pair, men's and women's, grouped into eras.

## Entity pages

- `https://padelticker.com/player/<id>` — one player: country, total matches, win-loss record, win rate, full match history and head-to-head. Example: /player/R000046842
- `https://padelticker.com/pair/<a>/<b>` — one partnership: matches together, record, rivals, every match as a team. Example: /pair/R000173623/R000189098
- `https://padelticker.com/tournament/<source>/<id>` — one tournament: draw, results and schedule. Example: /tournament/fip/229671
- `https://padelticker.com/national-teams/country/<cc>` — one nation's record across every championship.
- `https://padelticker.com/rankings/<fed>/<category>` — one ranking list, e.g. /rankings/DK/men.
- [Sitemap](https://padelticker.com/sitemap.xml) lists every entity page.

## Sources

Results are normalised from each federation's own published draws and scores through one
adapter layer: FIP (CUPRA FIP Tour and Premier Padel), RankedIn national tours, and
Dansk Padel Forbund. Rankings are the federations' published lists. Earnings are
estimated from published prize-money tables and draw placings, not reported by players,
and are labelled as estimates on the page.

## Related

- [Danske Padel Klip](https://danskepadelklip.com/): sister site, same author — Nordic-focused padel coverage, the FIP archive for Scandinavian players, and match clips. See https://danskepadelklip.com/llms.txt

## Optional

- /api/ is the app's own JSON and is disallowed in robots.txt: it is rate-limited and a
  crawl of it has taken the live site down. Read the rendered page instead; it carries
  the same facts.
- /privacy/, /terms/ and /streaming-tool/ belong to a separate streaming tool and are not
  about padel results.
